findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plaintext as Lambda environment variables in the Terraform source. Anyone with lambda:GetFunctionConfiguration, console read access, or access to the state file/repository can retrieve these long-lived credentials.

No kms_key_arn is configured, so the Lambda environment variables (which contain secrets) are encrypted only with the default AWS-managed key and are readable in cleartext by any principal able to describe the function. A customer-managed CMK with restricted key policy would provide an additional access-control boundary.
The function uses the nodejs12.x runtime, which has reached end of life and no longer receives security patches from AWS, leaving the execution environment exposed to known unpatched vulnerabilities.

The function has no vpc_config block, so it runs outside any customer VPC with unrestricted outbound internet access and no security group or network ACL boundary — enabling data exfiltration paths from compromised code holding the embedded credentials.
